title: The deadline one second past the bound let an admission decided after the bound count as admitted
resolution: The wait now reads a millisecond clock, EPOCHREALTIME or node, and ends exactly at the bound; a decision 1 ms after it is a timeout and 1 ms before it is admitted, which the draft and the base failed.

title: The regression test aligned the run to a wall-clock second and so still relied on the scheduler
resolution: A test-only clock seam runs the script on a fake clock moved only by fake sleep and node; the alignment and late-waking sleep are gone, and a whole-second clock fails the new tests on every run.

title: The recorded fail-before command restored the fixed script instead of the base
resolution: The fail-before now runs the new tests against the script of fa3fbce7, of the draft, and of a whole-second clock mutant, with the exact commands and output recorded.

title: The claim of about one second more latency ignored the poll and decision time
resolution: Every sleep is capped at the deadline and tested; design, proposal, and verification now state the latency with the read check and the decision time.

title: A clock that printed nothing made every deadline check false, so a hung read was never killed
resolution: clock_milliseconds accepts only digits and otherwise prints that the clock could not be read; the wait then exits with status 2, never the timeout 3. Two tests, an empty clock and one that stops printing a time, fail against de413797.

title: The capped-poll test could pass without ever reaching the capped poll
resolution: The test asserts that the sleeps add up to the bound exactly; a mutant whose cap sleeps 1 ms past the deadline fails it with 3001 against 3000.

title: Comment placeholders named SECONDS read as the bash variable behind the defect
resolution: The comments of deadline_in and sleep_within name the parameter N.

title: The follow-up cited line numbers of the draft, not of the base
resolution: design.md, tasks.md, and verification.md cite :505 and :519 at fa3fbce7 and function names otherwise; every cited line was checked.

title: A clock failure during a read exited the wait and left the read running
resolution: bounded_admission_read reads the clock itself; on a failure stop_read kills and reaps the read, and the wait exits with ADMISSION_CLOCK_FAILED. A new test that fails the clock during a read found the read still alive before the fix.

title: The capped-poll test could pass on read-loop sleeps alone, without the poll
resolution: The fake sleep waits until the fake reader has ended before it moves the clock; the test asserts the decision ran, no hung-read message, and sleeps of 3.000 or 1.000 then 2.000. A hanging-read mutant passes the old test and fails the new one, and so does an uncapped poll.

title: A clock command that failed but printed digits was accepted
resolution: clock_milliseconds fails when read_clock exits nonzero, whatever it printed; a new test with a clock that prints a time and exits 1 got status 0 before the fix and 2 after it.
